# Abstract

The Voynich Manuscript supports many mutually incompatible interpretations because surface regularity alone can be produced by language, cipher, or non-semantic procedures. We report a repository-wide attempt to replace plausibility judgments with held-out predictions and executable generative contracts. The canonical clean Takahashi H paragraph corpus contains 33,155 tokens and 6,870 types across 203 source locator identifiers, which aggregate to 188 page sides on 99 physical folios. Outer validation is grouped by physical bifolio, and alternative transcriptions of the same manuscript are treated as robustness tracks rather than independent replications. The strongest retained constraints are multiscale: physical lines and high-consensus spaces are structured boundaries; a first-order morphology transition kernel transfers across domains and Currier A/B; and predictive cache, integrated continuous state, morphology profiles, and a fully 80-token-independent production-image endpoint converge at physical-bifolio scope. The narrow H/80-token identity contrast retains its negative direction after exact same-quire, distance, hand, Currier, and domain matching, but support falls to 22 pairs/9 quires and the restricted test does not independently confirm it (`p=0.12099`). This leaves the cause of the retained bifolio-local state unresolved rather than eliminating the state. The first token has boundary-local composition without acting as a deterministic command, and exact-token realization benefits from narrow form-neighbourhood and parent-free character-legality channels. The retained constraints are integrated into Strong C v6/Q2, a normalized conditional-layout likelihood and sampler exposing fit, log-probability, sampling, ablation, and intervention. The model remains insufficient as a joint generator. Its long-range token-concentration shortfall survives five preregistered Taylor widths: at every width, 16/16 length-matched prose works beat token-frequency-preserving shuffle and empirical-bigram controls, and observed H exceeds all 256 v6 samples. Tests of direct substitutions, nomenclators, substitution-transposition cascades, fixed Naibbe v1, stable label-name mappings, several semantic image targets, and multiple residual repairs failed under their registered contracts. These failures are family-specific. No independent semantic variable currently beats the frozen surface model, no tested reversible cipher wins the full contract, and the strongest non-semantic baseline remains generatively incomplete. Therefore structured semantic system A, meaning-preserving cipher B, and meaningless structured generator C remain observationally unresolved.
**Keywords:** Voynich Manuscript; computational linguistics; physical codicology; held-out prediction; minimum description length; generative modeling; research-selection audit

# 1. Introduction

The Voynich Manuscript, Beinecke MS 408, combines an unidentified script with botanical, astronomical, biological, pharmaceutical, and other illustrations [1]. A long history of proposed readings has shown that local resemblance is cheap: a candidate can look linguistic, cryptographic, botanical, or procedural without predicting data that were not used to invent it. Reviews of computational work likewise emphasize that many global statistics are compatible with several origins [2,3].

This project asks a narrower and more falsifiable question. Which internal representations and generation rules survive physical grouping, held-out prediction, complexity costs, alternative transcription, and independent calibration? If a recoverable meaning layer exists, the same framework should eventually expose it through an independent semantic variable. Until that happens, surface fit is reported as surface fit.
We compare three broad upstream explanations:
- **A: structured semantic artificial system.** The observable text is generated from meaningful variables but need not be ordinary natural-language prose.
- **B: meaning-preserving natural-language cipher.** Plaintext passes through a reversible or preregistered lossy encoder before surface realization.
- **C: meaningless structured generator.** Structured output is produced without a semantic message.

All three feed the same downstream surface model. This design prevents a weak caricature of C from serving as the sole comparator for A or B. It also separates two questions that are often conflated: whether a model can reproduce selected regularities, and whether that model identifies the historical source.
[FIGURE:architecture]

The contributions of this report are fourfold. First, it fixes corpus and physical-unit contracts that prevent annotation deletion, locator mismatch, and page-level leakage. Second, it summarizes the retained multiscale constraints and their strongest countertests. Third, it describes an executable normalized surface baseline rather than a prose-only theory. Fourth, it accounts for research-wide adaptive selection, including failed families, so that repeated model search is visible rather than erased.
# 2. Evidence and falsification contract
## 2.1 Evidence classes

We distinguish direct manuscript observations, held-out predictions within the manuscript, robustness across alternative transcriptions, and independent external calibration. H, C, F, U, and V represent alternative readings of the same physical text. Concordant results across them can establish resistance to spacing, parsing, or glyph-reading choices. They cannot be counted as independent manuscripts, authors, contents, or corpus replications.

A physical holdout is distinct from an external replication. A complete unseen quire can test transfer within the manuscript while retaining manuscript-specific dependencies. An external book, manuscript, author/work group, or semantic annotation may provide independent evidence only when its provenance and selection are genuinely separate.
